full_judgment:
3. The defendant-opposite parties upon prayer for dismissal of the suit stated that the suit land belonged to government and it was leased out to the plaintiff-petitioners wrong-fully since the said land is high laying in nature and do not contain cultivable land and that the government has title and possession over the said land and the said khatian was cancelled on 25-3-2003 and the lease settlement was cancelled properly by issuing notice to the leasee plaintiffs. It is stated that the suit is not maintainable in this form and nature and it is barred by limitation and also stated other grounds in respect of dismissal of the plaintiffs's suit. 

 7. The ULAO of Goinghat Sadar Mr. Nripendra Kumar Das on behalf of the contesting defendants stated in his deposition that the suit land was leased out to the plaintiff Abdus Samad under Lease Case No.174 of 1991-92 but afterwards it was cancelled under Memo No.3225 of the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet for being the land non-cultivable in nature and the said cancellation was made following the proper procedure and the suit land is under the control of the government, but he admitted that the said land was mutated in the name of said leasee Abdus Samad and also stated that whoever only is landless and being in possession of the land is entitled to get lease of that land. The DW also stated that the value of the suit land has been increased a title due to establishment of Export-import Zone nearby. 

 9. Though the contesting defendants argued before the court of trial that the government announced that the suit land with other land as reserve forest, but in fact, they failed to submit any copy of gazette to prove such claim of them; rather the admittance of lease settlement of the suit land in the name of the plaintiff-petitioners is established by the written statement of the contesting defendants and also it appeared before the court of trial that the plaintiff-petitioners are in possession of the suit land and it was supported by the exhibits submitted by the plaintiff-petitioners. 

 The appellate court also imported a word the trial court dismissed the suit but not in the judgment of the trial court but stated the report of the UNO was not filed before the trial court and he could not consider that report and it void not binding upon the plaintiff. Thereafter report was produced before the appellate court. The appellate court mainly contended and quoted that the lease was given with certain conditions. There are 22 conditions in the lease, out of which condition No.21 they have violated. The appellate court quoted the condition No.21 which is mentioned herein below: — 

 14. This was the reason for cancelling the lease. It is also stated that the plaintiff failed to prove their case before the trial court. The appellate court in its judgment mainly relying upon the condition No. 21 Set-aside the judgment of the trial court for violating the condition. 

 16. On the other hand learned Deputy Attorney-General Abdul Wahab along with Ms. Shahana Parveen and Sanda Ghosh appearing on behalf of the opposite parties-Government very outset forcefully submitted that this Rule should be discharged on the ground that the kabuliyat executed in favour of the plaintiff-respondent-petitioners they have violated the conditions binding upon them. It is stated in the kabuliyat that if they violate any condition the deed will be cancelled. He read out the judgment of the appellate court and submits that there are 22 conditions, out of which they have violated the condition Nos.8 and 21. The condition No.21 has been quoted in the judgment of the appellate court and the condition No.8 is, without cultivating the leasee will not use the land for other purpose. But if the leasee has no land for living, in that case with written permission of the Deputy Commissioner he can use 008 acre of land as homestead. 

 17. But they have constructed the house on the land. Some of the land they have cultivated and some land they were using for their living purpose. For the above stated reasons the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet on relying upon the report of the UNO, Goainghat, Sylhet cancelled the lease. 

 "Lease or licence granted by the Government-Whether Government is entitled to deal with its property in any manner it likes or award a contract to any person it chooses without any constitutional limit upon it-Lease or licence to use Government property is a new property which is regulated by the state for the welfare of its people-Lease of fishery exclusively owned by the Government is a new kind of wealth which the Government distributes by way of settlement amongst the class of people who deserves it-In doing so Government was to enter into agreement but such lease agreement can by no stretch of imagination be termed as ordinary contract entered into by two individuals as trading venture-On the other hand when the Government deals with new kind of wealth for the welfare of the citizens and regulates distribution of such wealth by way of settlement or lease of the Government acts in its sovereign capacity-When authority oversteps or commits breach of rule or even in breach of principle of natural justice the same can be challenged by filing writ petition-State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1951 S.76-Government Estate Manuel 1958 Rr.205 & 206.
